en: Dependent on a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging (*upādinnupādāniya*) and is a root-cause (*hetu*), there arises a state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging and is not a root-cause, by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging and is a root-cause, there arises a state that is not acquired but subject to clinging and is not a root-cause, by way of the root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is both acquired and subject to clinging and is a root-cause, [there arises] a state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging...

A non-root phenomenon arises conditioned by a root cause. Dependent on a root phenomenon that is both acquired and subject to clinging (*upādinnupādāniya*), there arise phenomena that are neither acquired nor subject to clinging and are non-roots, as well as phenomena that are neither not-acquired-nor-not-subject-to-clinging and are non-roots, through the condition of a root cause.

Dependent on a root phenomenon that is both acquired and subject to clinging, there arise phenomena that are not not-acquired-but-subject-to-clinging and are non-roots, and phenomena that are neither not-acquired-nor-not-subject-to-clinging and are non-roots.
And states arise conditioned by a root-condition … five.

Dependent on a state that is not-clung-to but is-object-of-clinging and is a root, a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-object-of-clinging and is not-a-root arises conditioned by a root-condition … three.

Dependent on a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-object-of-clinging and is a root, a state that is neither-clung-to-nor-object-of-clinging and is not-a-root arises conditioned by a root-condition … five. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to root condition: thirteen; object condition: nine; predominance condition: eight ... [and so on] ... repetition condition: six ... [and so on] ... resultant condition: ten ... [and so on] ... non-disappearance condition: thirteen.

In dependence on a state that is acquired and subject to clinging (*upādinnupādāniya*) and is not a root (*nahetu*), there arises a state that is neither acquired nor subject to clinging (*naanupādinnupādāniya*) and is not a root (*nanahetu*), by way of root condition ...

three. (Abbreviated. With respect to root condition: nine; object condition: nine; predominance condition: six ... [and so on] ... repetition condition: six ... [and so on] ... resultant condition: six ... [and so on] ... non-disappearance condition: nine.
